newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sells 30 percent stake in fertiliser firm.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sells 30 percent stake in fertiliser firm.

text.p: Morocco's privatisation minister on Monday announced the sale of 30 percent of the capital of fertiliser firm Fertima.

The public offer, of 690,000 shares priced at 174 dirhams ($20) per share will open on 15 October and run to 22 October, and go on the Casablanca bourse on October 29, minister Abderrahman Saaidi told a news conference.
"It is the 45th transfer operation, excluding those of (four) mines. It is also the 11th through the Casablanca bourse and the sixth biggest privatisation operation," Saadi said.
The offer is open equally to Moroccans and foreign investors.
Societe Marocaine des Fertilisants (Fertima), registered a turnover of 787 million dirhams in 1995 from 925 million dirhams the year before. The fall in turnover was attributable to a severe drought.
The company, which blends and markets fertilisers and holds more than 60 percent of the market, posted a pre-tax profit of 68 million dirhams in 1995 from 33 million the previous year.

It forecasts domestic yearly consumption of fertilisers by the year 2000 to increase by two percent in case of drought and four percent with a normal rainfall to between 820,000 and 900,000 tonnes from the current 0.7 and 0.8 million tonnes.
The company employs 373 people, operates 10 factories and 11 warehouses.
Fertima, whose capital was increased by incorporating reserves in 1996 to 115 million dirhams, was established in 1972 and is an offshoot of the state-owned Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP).
